checks: Compared all decoded fields of the original and revised candidates. The only edit is a replacement within the final statement sentence that names the two attained quantities. The proof hash, source metadata and dependency IDs are unchanged.

Rechecked the binary-product sharpness example. Only the two caps assigned to a given binary base meet that fiber. Each covers a central half-body of mass V/2, so every cap is necessary and V/2=M/(2k). The statement now confines the attainment claim to these two quantities.
Independently recalculated the same-wave predecessor's frozen bytes, statement and proof hashes and matched them against its approval. Its exact-cover hypothesis still applies with t=2.
Checked 05b459fea3722ebb §§1–2 and 5–6, including (1)–(2), and ed1a79b6ef1fd236 §5. Both sharpness calculations attain M/(2k), and the latter uses the same construction for proper partitions.

A full-measure closed trace covers its whole convex fiber because a nonempty relatively open missed part has positive intrinsic volume. Otherwise positive finite weighted incidence forces a proper positive trace whose boundary cuts the relative interior.

On the chosen restricted hyperplane a point away from all noncoincident boundaries exists by their lower affine dimension, including dimension one where the different boundary points are disjoint. The weighted scores in the two adjacent open half-balls must agree because they are constant on each half-ball and agree with b_z almost everywhere. The initial positive weight forces an opposite cap with the same restricted plane. Those two original traces cover the whole affine plane.

Apply the same-batch original-cap result with t=2. The selected caps cover all measured fibers, the other integer fibers have zero q-measure, and subadditivity gives the lower bound M/(2k) on the largest original mass.

The binomial expansion gives (1+1/d)^d at least 2, strictly greater for d>=2. With k<=2^n this proves the comparison with gamma_d M/2^n. Unit weights give the partition case, where every omitted positive cap would have positive mass outside the selected union.

On a binary product, q_p is zero at its own base and at least one at every other base. The chosen A makes each original cap empty at the other bases. Reflection x to -x exchanges the central cuts, and their overlap is a null hyperplane. Thus all 2k caps are indispensable and each has mass V/2=M/(2k), with k=2^n.
